title: Watari-ago-shikuchi
guidance: A post carries a stepped tenon: a flat plate that sits in a blind mortise under the 桁 girder, and a square tenon above it that rises through the girder and the 梁 beam and ends flush with the beam's top.  The girder's top carries a raised rib either side of the tenon, a little narrower than the girder, and the beam's underside is notched at both edges to take them; the central tab between the ribs locks the beam against twisting and takes load off the tenon.  Drawn from @thejoinery_jp's assembly GIF (tweet 771307153583812610).

usage: Post, 桁 girder and 梁 beam crossing in one stack: the post's stepped tenon (a flat plate under the girder, a square above) rises through girder and beam and ends flush with the beam's top, and two ribs on the girder's top fit notches under the beam either side of the tenon.
strengths: The plate tenon seats the girder on the post; the square tenon ties all three timbers in line and resists uplift.
The two ribs lock the beam between them, so it cannot twist or wander and the tenon carries little of the load.
weaknesses: The square hole is cut through both horizontal timbers and must be set out with the hook and notch together.
The hook, notch and side slot are read from one isometric view of the GIF, so their depths are approximate.
